Lipids
The lipid content of vegetables is very low (0.1–1% of fresh weight). It consists of triacylglycerols, glucolipids, and phospholipids.
They have saturated, monounsaturated, and polyunsaturated fatty acids.
Vitamins
Vegetables are characterized by the supply of fat-soluble and water-soluble vitamins. The type, variety, and conditions before and
after harvest, storage, and technological or culinary treatments inﬂuence the vitamin content. Some are an important source of
vitamin A (in the form of its precursors, carotenoids), vitamin C, and folic acid (Table 5). They also contain other fat-soluble
